title: Language adapter
description: Everything the toolkit knows about one language. No script, workflow or agent may hardcode a file extension, an annotation syntax or a build command; all three come from here. Adding a language means adding one file in adapters/ and one directory in rules/, and changing nothing else.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editor completion. Ignored by the loader.

id.description: Stable machine identifier. Must equal the file's basename: adapters/<id>.json.

displayName.description: Human label used in reports and CI job names.

detect.description: Globs whose presence in a project activates this adapter. Choose markers that are specific to the stack: a project file, not a source file.

detectUnless.description: Globs whose presence DEACTIVATES this adapter, even when 'detect' matched. For a marker that a more specific adapter also owns: every TypeScript project has a package.json, so the JavaScript adapter must stand down when a tsconfig.json is present, or both would run the identical commands twice. Use sparingly — a stack that genuinely needs two adapters should get both.

testGlobs.description: Where tests live. The traceability checker scans exactly these files for @covers annotations.

ignore.description: Build output and vendored directories to exclude from every scan. These are language-specific (bin/obj, node_modules, target) and therefore belong here rather than in a shared list.

pattern.description: Regular expression locating a test annotation. It MUST expose exactly two capture groups: group 1 the requirement id, group 2 the version digits. Group 2 should be optional so that an annotation missing its mandatory @v is reported as a violation rather than silently ignored (CONVENTIONS.md §5).

example.description: A literal annotation as written in this language. It must match `pattern`; the loader checks this.

commands.description: Shell commands run by the CI gates. The first four are required: a stack with no linter should say so explicitly rather than leave the field out.

format.description: Rewrite one file in place. Used by the format hook, not by CI. Include the token {file}; the hook substitutes the path. Optional: an adapter with no formatter is skipped, not failed.

integration.description: Integration and contract tests, run at gate G4. Optional: a project with none skips G4 rather than failing it. Kept separate from `test` because G4 runs after G1-G3 have passed, and integration suites are slow enough that ordering matters.

testFiles.description: Run ONLY the named test files. The selected paths are appended as arguments, space-separated, so this must be a command that accepts file paths last. Used by G2 and G4 to run a derived regression scope when the pull request declares REQ- or CHG- ids. OPTIONAL, and its absence is a supported answer, not a gap: a stack whose runner selects by fully-qualified test name rather than by file (dotnet test --filter, for one) has no honest way to express this, and the gates run the full suite instead. Never approximate it — a scoped run that silently misses tests is worse than a slow one.

integrationFiles.description: The same idea for gate G4's integration suite. Optional, and subject to the same rule: absent means G4 runs everything.

ci.description: How CI obtains this language's toolchain. GitHub Actions does not allow an expression in `uses:`, so a workflow cannot choose setup-dotnet or setup-java dynamically — but `container:` DOES accept one. Declaring the image here is therefore the only way a single gates.yml can serve any language without editing.

container.description: Docker image carrying this language's toolchain, e.g. mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0. Pin a major version; do not use `latest`.

rules.description: Repository-relative path to this language's coding rules, shipped into .claude/rules/ by the installer.

glob.description: Forward-slash glob. Backslashes are rejected so that adapters behave identically on Windows and Linux.
